project: Titanic source-first lifeboat equipment and evacuation chapter

shots.editorial_why: Genuine pre-sinking second-class boat-deck photograph establishing installed equipment, NOT a photograph of launch or count.
Sourced exact boat categories and rated figures need a legible mathematical diagram; archival photo alone cannot prove quantity.

shots.onscreen_label: EARLY BOARD OF TRADE LIFEBOAT RULES
shots.editorial_why: Original data-based rule table distinguishes dated regulations; a historic photo cannot depict exact legal tonnage breakpoints.

shots.onscreen_label: THE RULES DID NOT MATCH BIGGER LINERS
shots.editorial_why: Explicit original capacity graph, not a fabricated photo of the Board of Trade report.

shots.onscreen_label: ACTUAL RESCUE PHOTOS — CARPATHIA AFTER SINKING
shots.editorial_why: Original period photos of lifeboats near the receiving ship show real transfer context; NOT evidence of early evacuation plans.
Period photo of actual recovered boats on rescue ship shows boat-transfer function, not hypothetical past transfer success.
Real shipboard area and davits provide authentic operational setting before life-saving equipment was readied.
No surviving original Titanic launch footage; technical process needs clearly labelled non-footage diagram.

shots.onscreen_label: VIEW FROM TITANIC BOAT DECK — 3 APRIL 1912
shots.editorial_why: Contemporary real onboard photograph supplies scale and access context, not proof of exact position numbers.

shots.onscreen_label: COLLAPSIBLE A, B, C AND D / SCHEMATIC
shots.editorial_why: Original deck positioning is communicated by sourced diagram, not inventing a historic labelled photograph.

shots.onscreen_label: LIFEBOATS ON WAY TO CARPATHIA / 15 APRIL 1912
shots.editorial_why: A real post-sinking photo illustrates Titanic lifeboats but NOT how many seats were used at departure.
Source-labelled numerical findings from inquiry; caption clarifies no historic photograph proves departure occupancy.
Louis Ogden genuine 1912 photograph of real boat, shown as physical equipment—not specific forty-person emergency cutter.
No original visual evidence of crews' uncertainty at launching; use one clear sourced explanatory chart.
Real period U.S. Senate inquiry witness image establishes post-disaster evidence collection; not photograph of launch clock.
Explicit source-anchored uncertainty graphic, avoiding falsely exact timestamp claims.

shots.onscreen_label: REAL TITANIC LIFEBOATS / PHOTOGRAPHED AFTER RESCUE
shots.editorial_why: Further distinct authentic period rescue photograph anchors subsequent improvements in life-saving systems.
Dated regulatory milestones must be presented in a labelled timeline, not a generic promotional slide.

shots.onscreen_label: RMS TITANIC BEFORE CROSSING THE ATLANTIC
shots.editorial_why: Correct dated pre-disaster vessel image sets calm voyage scene before ice warning topic.
Different contemporary Titanic voyage photograph gives human context before April 14 warning narrative.

rights_note: Research source/rights/shaft/davits individually. All rescue photographs labelled POST-SINKING, never launch images. Diagrams explain impossible photographic content.
